samples.summary: Two other `docSplitBlock` callers still ignore the empty-list-item short-circuit the diff worked around in `insertBlocks`
samples.evidence:
`insertBlocks` now special-cases `Doc.splitBlock`'s empty-list-item short-circuit (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3609-3626, and the branch itself at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:303-307, which the diff changed to exit into a *heading*). Two sibling callers of the same primitive were not audited:

- `handlePageBreak` — packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2141-2147: `const newBlockId = this.docSplitBlock(pos.blockId, pos.offset)` followed by `blocks.findIndex(b => b.id === newBlockId)` / `insertBlockAt(splitIndex, pageBreakBlock)`. On an empty list item the split returns the *same* id, so `splitIndex` is the caret's own block and the page break is inserted *before* it instead of after; with this change the bullet is simultaneously promoted to `heading` (`unlistedBlockType`) rather than `paragraph`, so Ctrl+Enter on an empty bulleted heading now leaves a Heading block below a page break.
- `insertPlainText` — packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3536-3540: same call in the newline loop. When the pasted text begins with a newline and the caret sits in an empty bullet, the first split short-circuits, the leading empty line is swallowed, and (new with this change) the bullet becomes a `heading`, so the following pasted body text is rendered as Heading N.

The fix belongs either at these two call sites (mirroring the `splitExitsList` branch the diff added) or by moving that handling into `docSplitBlock` so every caller benefits.

samples.summary: Enter inside a table cell keeps the old assumption that `docSplitBlock` always returns a new block id
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2085-2089 (`handleEnter`'s table-cell branch) does `const newBlockId = this.docSplitBlock(pos.blockId, pos.offset); this.cursor.moveTo({ blockId: newBlockId, offset: 0 })` with no `newBlockId === pos.blockId` guard — unlike the top-level branch at 2118-2125, which has one. For an empty `list-item` inside a table cell, `Doc.splitBlock` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:303-307, changed by this diff) now exits the list into a `heading` and returns the same id; the caret is silently re-homed to offset 0 of a block that just changed type, and no new block is created even though the code below marks the table dirty as if it had split. Behaviourally close to the desired list exit, but the assumption is now demonstrably wrong on this path and the cell branch was not considered alongside the `insertBlocks` fix.

finding.summary: `insertPlainText` still hits the `Doc.splitBlock` empty-list-item short-circuit that `insertBlocks` was just patched to avoid — and the diff makes that short-circuit convert the block to a heading
finding.evidence: The diff adds a workaround in `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3610-3626) because `Doc.splitBlock` returns the *same* block id for an empty list item instead of splitting (document.ts:303-307). The sibling caller `insertPlainText` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3536) was not updated: with the caret in an empty bullet, `docSplitBlock` returns the same id, the cursor is moved to offset 0 of that same block, and every subsequent line is prepended into one block — multi-line plain-text paste (Ctrl+Shift+V / `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`, text-editor.ts:3498-3510) collapses and reverses the lines. This change additionally makes that short-circuit convert an empty *bulleted heading* into a `heading` block (document.ts:301-307), so the same paste now also silently promotes the destination to Heading N. `ensureEditableBlock` (line 3520) is unaffected (hr/page-break only) and `editor.ts:3258/3277` are guarded by `offset > 0 && offset < len`.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present and unguarded. `Doc.splitBlock` short-circuits on an empty `list-item` by calling `setBlockType(unlistedBlockType(block))` and returning the SAME block id (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:303-307), and `unlistedBlockType` yields `heading` when `headingLevel` is remembered (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:337-344). `insertBlocks` was patched for exactly this case (text-editor.ts:3609-3627), but the sibling caller `insertPlainText` was not: text-editor.ts:3536-3540 calls the thin wrapper `docSplitBlock` (text-editor.ts:403-407) and then moves the cursor to offset 0 of what may be the same block, so the line boundary is lost and the destination block's type silently changes. No guard blocks it — `ensureEditableBlock` (text-editor.ts:3516-3523) only handles horizontal-rule/page-break. The path is reachable from Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+V (text-editor.ts:1054-1057 -> 3498-3510) and from the plain-text fallback of the normal paste path (text-editor.ts:1190-1194). Triggering inputs exist: multi-line text starting with a newline pasted into an empty bullet, or any multi-line paste containing a blank line where the preceding split creates a fresh empty `list-item` (document.ts:330-331). The reviewer's "reverses the lines" wording overstates the impact (after the first short-circuit the block is no longer a list-item, so later splits behave normally), but that is impact detail, not presence; the changed-contract-with-unupdated-caller is real and in the blast-radius lane at major.

finding.summary: The slides clipboard reaches the same docs `Block` model with no validation, bypassing the new `deserializeBlocks` sanitizer's threat model
finding.evidence: The diff hardens the docs internal clipboard because "any page can put [it] on the system clipboard" and unvalidated values flow "straight into the shared Yorkie tree, the renderer, and the DOCX/PDF exporters" (clipboard.ts:34-43). `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-49` parses a JSON payload, checks only a `magic` string, and returns `parsed.elements as Element[]`; `Element` carries `blocks: Block[]` of the identical docs model (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1,265). It is reached from the paste handler at packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:819 and — worse — from `tryDeserialize` on the plain `text/plain` flavour at keyboard.ts:847, which any page can write. Those blocks are rendered by the shared docs text-box renderer and exported (PPTX/PDF), so the class of injection the diff closes for docs remains open one package over. Fix belongs on the slides deserializer (reuse a shared block sanitizer).

verdict.reason: Verified the absence claim directly. packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/clipboard.ts:38-58 parses clipboard JSON and returns `parsed.elements` after checking only the `magic` string and `Array.isArray(elements)` — no per-element or per-block shape validation. Those elements carry `TextBody.blocks: Block[]` of the exact docs model imported from `@wafflebase/docs` (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:1,263-265), the model the diff's `sanitizeBlocks` was written to rebuild from untrusted JSON (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:22-30,36-43). The payload is attacker-writable: `readClipboard` falls back to the plain `text/plain` flavour (keyboard.ts:823-829, 836-837) and `tryDeserialize` (keyboard.ts:845-851) accepts it, feeding Cmd+V (keyboard.ts:343-362) straight into `pasteElements`. Nothing downstream validates: paste.ts:51-70 only spreads the source and offsets the frame, and store/memory.ts:558-593 `addElement` only clones and recomputes connector frames. I searched packages/slides/src (and its store) for sanitiz/normaliz/validate/schema/zod/assert and found only unrelated PPTX/geometry normalisation; no slides-side block or element sanitizer exists anywhere, and nothing in slides imports `deserializeBlocks`/`deserializeClipboard`. The only place the new sanitizer does cover slides is in-text-box paste via docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1240-1259, which is a different entry point and does not guard the element-level canvas paste path. Unvalidated blocks therefore reach the shared docs-derived text renderer (slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:247-261) and helpers that dereference `b.inlines` unguarded (model/element.ts:638-655), i.e. a reachable alternate entry point into the same shared model the diff hardened. Real and blocking under the blast-radius rubric (major).
